subject.title: [Feature]: Pluggable STT backend for macOS Push-to-Talk

question: Should native macOS Push-to-Talk get its own batch STT backend boundary that can call Gateway media audio or local/private ASR, and how should provider selection, credentials, private-network access, and fallback be owned?
rationale: The missing capability is clear in source, but the durable fix crosses macOS app code, Gateway media-understanding providers, auth/config, microphone privacy, local-network security, and user-visible fallback behavior.

options.title: Design a narrow batch PTT backend
options.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default, add an explicit batch-only backend capability for native PTT, and require provider/auth/error-state tests before implementation.

options.title: Fold into broader custom ASR design
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/46661 the canonical design surface only if the native PTT capture-boundary requirements from this issue are preserved there.

options.title: Defer native PTT backend work
options.body: Keep sidecar or plugin workarounds for now and avoid expanding the native app's transcription/config surface until provider capability routing is settled.

recommendation.title: Design a narrow batch PTT backend
recommendation.body: Keep Apple Speech as the default, add an explicit batch-only backend capability for native PTT, and require provider/auth/error-state tests before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest sampled native voice feature-history signal and is already routed in the issue timeline for this topic.
